input.patchText:
*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: out/build_outputs.py
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import duckdb
+import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
+import pandas as pd
+
+
+OUT = Path("out")
+SOURCE = "data/crashes.parquet"
+
+annual = duckdb.sql(
+    f"""
+    SELECT year(crash_date) AS year,
+           SUM(number_of_pedestrians_killed)::INTEGER AS pedestrians_killed
+    FROM read_parquet('{SOURCE}')
+    WHERE year(crash_date) BETWEEN 2013 AND 2025
+    GROUP BY year
+    ORDER BY year
+    """
+).df()
+borough = duckdb.sql(
+    f"""
+    SELECT year(crash_date) AS year,
+           COALESCE(borough, 'Unknown / missing') AS borough,
+           SUM(number_of_pedestrians_killed)::INTEGER AS pedestrians_killed
+    FROM read_parquet('{SOURCE}')
+    WHERE year(crash_date) BETWEEN 2013 AND 2025
+    GROUP BY year, borough
+    ORDER BY year, borough
+    """
+).df()
+
+years = list(range(2013, 2026))
+assert annual["year"].tolist() == years
+assert annual["pedestrians_killed"].sum() == borough["pedestrians_killed"].sum()
+assert borough.groupby("year")["pedestrians_killed"].sum().reindex(years).tolist() == annual[
+    "pedestrians_killed"
+].tolist()
+
+annual.to_csv(OUT / "values_1.csv", index=False)
+annual.to_csv(OUT / "values_2.csv", index=False)
+borough.to_csv(OUT / "values_3.csv", index=False)
+
+plt.figure(figsize=(10, 5.5))
+plt.plot(annual["year"], annual["pedestrians_killed"], marker="o", linewidth=2, color="#176B87")
+for row in annual.itertuples(index=False):
+    plt.annotate(str(row.pedestrians_killed), (row.year, row.pedestrians_killed),
+                 xytext=(0, 8), textcoords="offset points", ha="center", fontsize=8)
+plt.xticks(years, rotation=45)
+plt.ylabel("Pedestrians killed")
+plt.xlabel("Crash year")
+plt.title("Pedestrians killed in NYC motor vehicle crashes by year")
+plt.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.25)
+plt.tight_layout()
+plt.savefig(OUT / "option_1.png", dpi=180)
+plt.close()
+
+plt.figure(figsize=(10, 5.5))
+bars = plt.bar(annual["year"].astype(str), annual["pedestrians_killed"], color="#D97732")
+plt.bar_label(bars, padding=3, fontsize=8)
+plt.ylabel("Pedestrians killed")
+plt.xlabel("Crash year")
+plt.title("Annual number of pedestrians killed in NYC motor vehicle crashes")
+plt.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.25)
+plt.tight_layout()
+plt.savefig(OUT / "option_2.png", dpi=180)
+plt.close()
+
+borough_order = ["BRONX", "BROOKLYN", "MANHATTAN", "QUEENS", "STATEN ISLAND", "Unknown / missing"]
+pivot = borough.pivot(index="year", columns="borough", values="pedestrians_killed").reindex(
+    index=years, columns=borough_order, fill_value=0
+).fillna(0)
+colors = ["#477998", "#E07A5F", "#81B29A", "#F2CC8F", "#8D6A9F", "#A8A8A8"]
+ax = pivot.plot(kind="bar", stacked=True, figsize=(11, 6), color=colors, width=0.78)
+ax.set_ylabel("Pedestrians killed")
+ax.set_xlabel("Crash year")
+ax.set_title("Annual pedestrian fatalities by recorded borough")
+ax.legend(title="Borough", bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc="upper left", frameon=False)
+ax.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.25)
+plt.xticks(rotation=45)
+plt.tight_layout()
+plt.savefig(OUT / "option_3.png", dpi=180, bbox_inches="tight")
+plt.close()
+
+def annual_values_sentence():
+    return "; ".join(
+        f"{row.year}: {row.pedestrians_killed}" for row in annual.itertuples(index=False)
+    )
+
+
+values = annual_values_sentence()
+options = {
+    "options": [
+        {
+            "id": 1,
+            "metric": "Annual number of pedestrians killed",
+            "denominator": "None (raw count)",
+            "grouping": "Crash year, 2013–2025",
+            "chart_type": "Line chart",
+            "reason": "A line chart makes year-to-year changes in the annual fatality count easy to follow.",
+            "probability": 0.4,
+            "answer": f"Pedestrians killed by crash year: {values}.",
+        },
+        {
+            "id": 2,
+            "metric": "Annual number of pedestrians killed",
+            "denominator": "None (raw count)",
+            "grouping": "Crash year, 2013–2025",
+            "chart_type": "Vertical bar chart",
+            "reason": "Bars emphasize the absolute number in each distinct calendar year and support direct comparisons between years.",
+            "probability": 0.35,
+            "answer": f"The yearly counts are: {values}.",
+        },
+        {
+            "id": 3,
+            "metric": "Annual number of pedestrians killed, partitioned by recorded borough",
+            "denominator": "None (raw counts; borough stacks sum to the annual citywide count)",
+            "grouping": "Crash year and borough, with missing borough recorded as Unknown / missing",
+            "chart_type": "Stacked vertical bar chart",
+            "reason": "The borough stacks retain the annual citywide totals while showing how the recorded geography contributes to each total.",
+            "probability": 0.25,
+            "answer": f"Summing the borough segments gives these NYC annual totals (including crashes with unknown or missing borough): {values}.",
+        },
+    ]
+}
+(OUT / "options.json").write_text(json.dumps(options, indent=2) + "\n")
*** End Patch

+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import duckdb
+import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
+import pandas as pd
+
+
+OUT = Path("out")
+SOURCE = "data/crashes.parquet"
+
+annual = duckdb.sql(
+    f"""
+    SELECT year(crash_date) AS year,
+           SUM(number_of_pedestrians_killed)::INTEGER AS pedestrians_killed
+    FROM read_parquet('{SOURCE}')
+    WHERE year(crash_date) BETWEEN 2013 AND 2025
+    GROUP BY year
+    ORDER BY year
+    """
+).df()
+borough = duckdb.sql(
+    f"""
+    SELECT year(crash_date) AS year,
+           COALESCE(borough, 'Unknown / missing') AS borough,
+           SUM(number_of_pedestrians_killed)::INTEGER AS pedestrians_killed
+    FROM read_parquet('{SOURCE}')
+    WHERE year(crash_date) BETWEEN 2013 AND 2025
+    GROUP BY year, borough
+    ORDER BY year, borough
+    """
+).df()
+
+years = list(range(2013, 2026))
+assert annual["year"].tolist() == years
+assert annual["pedestrians_killed"].sum() == borough["pedestrians_killed"].sum()
+assert borough.groupby("year")["pedestrians_killed"].sum().reindex(years).tolist() == annual[
+    "pedestrians_killed"
+].tolist()
+
+annual.to_csv(OUT / "values_1.csv", index=False)
+annual.to_csv(OUT / "values_2.csv", index=False)
+borough.to_csv(OUT / "values_3.csv", index=False)
+
+plt.figure(figsize=(10, 5.5))
+plt.plot(annual["year"], annual["pedestrians_killed"], marker="o", linewidth=2, color="#176B87")
+for row in annual.itertuples(index=False):
+    plt.annotate(str(row.pedestrians_killed), (row.year, row.pedestrians_killed),
+                 xytext=(0, 8), textcoords="offset points", ha="center", fontsize=8)
+plt.xticks(years, rotation=45)
+plt.ylabel("Pedestrians killed")
+plt.xlabel("Crash year")
+plt.title("Pedestrians killed in NYC motor vehicle crashes by year")
+plt.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.25)
+plt.tight_layout()
+plt.savefig(OUT / "option_1.png", dpi=180)
+plt.close()
+
+plt.figure(figsize=(10, 5.5))
+bars = plt.bar(annual["year"].astype(str), annual["pedestrians_killed"], color="#D97732")
+plt.bar_label(bars, padding=3, fontsize=8)
+plt.ylabel("Pedestrians killed")
+plt.xlabel("Crash year")
+plt.title("Annual number of pedestrians killed in NYC motor vehicle crashes")
+plt.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.25)
+plt.tight_layout()
+plt.savefig(OUT / "option_2.png", dpi=180)
+plt.close()
+
+borough_order = ["BRONX", "BROOKLYN", "MANHATTAN", "QUEENS", "STATEN ISLAND", "Unknown / missing"]
+pivot = borough.pivot(index="year", columns="borough", values="pedestrians_killed").reindex(
+    index=years, columns=borough_order, fill_value=0
+).fillna(0)
+colors = ["#477998", "#E07A5F", "#81B29A", "#F2CC8F", "#8D6A9F", "#A8A8A8"]
+ax = pivot.plot(kind="bar", stacked=True, figsize=(11, 6), color=colors, width=0.78)
+ax.set_ylabel("Pedestrians killed")
+ax.set_xlabel("Crash year")
+ax.set_title("Annual pedestrian fatalities by recorded borough")
+ax.legend(title="Borough", bbox_to_anchor=(1.02, 1), loc="upper left", frameon=False)
+ax.grid(axis="y", alpha=0.25)
+plt.xticks(rotation=45)
+plt.tight_layout()
+plt.savefig(OUT / "option_3.png", dpi=180, bbox_inches="tight")
+plt.close()
+
+def annual_values_sentence():
+    return "; ".join(
+        f"{row.year}: {row.pedestrians_killed}" for row in annual.itertuples(index=False)
+    )
+
+
+values = annual_values_sentence()
+options = {
+    "options": [
+        {
+            "id": 1,
+            "metric": "Annual number of pedestrians killed",
+            "denominator": "None (raw count)",
+            "grouping": "Crash year, 2013–2025",
+            "chart_type": "Line chart",
+            "reason": "A line chart makes year-to-year changes in the annual fatality count easy to follow.",
+            "probability": 0.4,
+            "answer": f"Pedestrians killed by crash year: {values}.",
+        },
+        {
+            "id": 2,
+            "metric": "Annual number of pedestrians killed",
+            "denominator": "None (raw count)",
+            "grouping": "Crash year, 2013–2025",
+            "chart_type": "Vertical bar chart",
+            "reason": "Bars emphasize the absolute number in each distinct calendar year and support direct comparisons between years.",
+            "probability": 0.35,
+            "answer": f"The yearly counts are: {values}.",
+        },
+        {
+            "id": 3,
+            "metric": "Annual number of pedestrians killed, partitioned by recorded borough",
+            "denominator": "None (raw counts; borough stacks sum to the annual citywide count)",
+            "grouping": "Crash year and borough, with missing borough recorded as Unknown / missing",
+            "chart_type": "Stacked vertical bar chart",
+            "reason": "The borough stacks retain the annual citywide totals while showing how the recorded geography contributes to each total.",
+            "probability": 0.25,
+            "answer": f"Summing the borough segments gives these NYC annual totals (including crashes with unknown or missing borough): {values}.",
+        },
+    ]
+}
+(OUT / "options.json").write_text(json.dumps(options, indent=2) + "\n")
